thread:
maya: heads-up — after the runtime tweak to async prefetch last night we're seeing a 5-8% p99 latency regression on multi-GPU TP runs for our fused-attn models. repro on staging with tp=4, pp=1.

maya: quick perf snippet from perf traces (layer 23):
```
all_gather: 1.8ms  | compute_idle: 0.9ms | compute_active: 2.2ms
qkv_pack: 0.4ms    | flash_attn_kernel: 6.1ms
small_message_churn: ~12 msgs/layer per rank
```

maya: looks like we got a lot of small all_gather calls instead of a single consolidated one — messages are fragmented because q/k/v stripe sizes aren't uniform (split-stripe) when seq_len%tp != 0.

liam: ugh, I suspected the prefetch change might reorder the scatter/gather windows. that fragmentation can kill comm/compute overlap.

liam: two quick ideas: 1) change kernel selection to prefer an unpacked QKV path that does a single per-layer all_gather when stripe_small_ratio > 0.2; 2) or add a lightweight padding heuristic to make stripe sizes uniform at runtime.

arjun: +1 on both. flash_attn prefers packed QKV for perf but only when layout is contiguous. when splitstripe happens we either do N small alls or fallback. we should measure the break-even: cost(padding) vs cost(many small alls).

casey: on batching heuristics side — we can bias microbatch grouping to preserve stripe alignment (e.g., pad batch to next lcm(seq_len, tp) multiple). cheap to do in request-router before the runtime picks kernels. downside: extra tokens => cost.

perf-bot: linked regression ticket #R-4721 (added traces + flamegraphs). Note: similar symptom observed in 1766004321 but different root cause.

maya: ran a quick A/B on staging: implement runtime padding of qkv shards to nearest divisible chunk (cheap memcpy) + single all_gather per layer. results: p99 down 7% on same workload, throughput -1.4% (due to memcpy), cpu spin negligible.

maya: new perf snippet after patch:
```
all_gather: 0.9ms  | compute_idle: 0.3ms | compute_active: 2.1ms
qkv_pack: 0.6ms    | flash_attn_kernel: 6.0ms
small_message_churn: ~1 msg/layer per rank
```

liam: nice. that suggests fragmentation > padding cost. we should land a configurable switch: runtime.prefetch.splitstripe_padding = true/false and default to true for TP>1.

arjun: also - update kernel picker heuristic to prefer contiguous layout kernels only when stripe_small_ratio < 0.15; else prefer consolidated comm path. avoids flip-flopping on edge cases.

casey: canary plan? we should roll to dedicated staging first then 10% of prod TP clusters, watch p99, token cost, and KV cache hit rate. add metric: all_gather_count_per_layer and avg_msg_size.

liam: PR up: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/3398 — small runtime change + config flag + tests.

deploy-bot: started canary deploy to staging (canary id: canary-3398). monitoring dashboards: /d/stg/tp-fused-attn.

maya: will collect 12h canary stats and post. next steps: if stable, add permanent kernel-picker rule and a lightweight telemetry event for splitstripe occurrences.

liam: also add a unit test that simulates uneven seq_len patterns so we don't regresses back to fragmented alls.

maya: thanks — appreciate quick triage. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: reminder: include perf traces and raw nvprof snippets in the PR description.

casey: noted. I'll add the batching heuristic doc in the ops-runbook for TP clusters.

maya: (update 1881002420) 6h canary looks good — p99 back to baseline on staging. moving to 10% prod next hour.
